title: 6061-T6 vs T651 vs T6511: Which Temper Do You Actually Need?
summary: T6, T651 and T6511 are the same alloy in three conditions. T651 is stress-relieved plate and cold-finished bar, T6511 is stress-relieved extrusions. Here is which one your print needs and why the minimums differ.
body_markdown:
### What is the difference between 6061-T6 and 6061-T651?


T651 receives the same solution-treatment and artificial-aging basis as T6, with a controlled stretch after solution treatment to reduce residual quench stress before aging. For a given product form and dimension range, the specified strengths can match, while the stress relief improves machining stability. T651 is the normal temper for rolled plate.


### What is the difference between T651 and T6511?


Product form. T651 applies to rolled plate and cold-finished bar; T6511 applies to extruded bar, rod, and shapes with minor straightening permitted after stretching. Guaranteed properties then depend on the product specification and dimension: the referenced extrusion is 38,000 psi ultimate, cold-finished bar is 42,000 psi, and ASTM B209 T651 plate is 42,000 psi through 4 inches and 40,000 psi at 4.001–6 inches.


### Is T6511 stronger than T6?


No. They have the same specified strength for a given product form. T6511 adds stress relief, which is about dimensional stability during machining rather than about strength.


### Can I substitute 6061-T6511 bar for a 6061-T651 callout?


Not without engineering and specification review. They are different product forms with different guaranteed properties, tolerances, and test orientations. A shared cited longitudinal yield minimum is not enough to approve a substitution; the drawing authority must verify form, governing specification, dimension range, orientation, fatigue and toughness requirements, and certification.


### Which 6061 temper is best for machining?


Any stress-relieved temper: T651 for plate and cold-finished bar, T6511 for extrusions. Plain T6 without stress relief is the one to avoid for parts with heavy or asymmetric material removal, because the part will move as you cut.
